bug_semantics: ChaiScript's script-visible async() launched a callable with std::async(std::launch::async, ...) but the ChaiScript/Dispatch_Engine did not own or join the resulting worker. A script could start asynchronous work and finish while that work was still resolving identifiers. Engine teardown on the main thread then freed shared Dispatch_Engine state, including map nodes in the symbol/object tables, while a worker still used that state. A subsequent heterogeneous std::map lookup read a freed std::string key through chaiscript::str_less::operator(), producing the reported heap-use-after-free. str_less is the observed ASan crash site, not the causal ownership defect. The issue #632 PoC launches two async functions that repeatedly access undefined re6 and then lets the script end without waiting for the futures, creating the teardown/read race.
flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2, which first added future support and registered script async() as a direct std::async(std::launch::async, t_func) call in include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp without engine lifetime tracking or a teardown join. Its sole parent a32a180a063d9186ca38b2708a9c19d50da378db has no <future> include, future type, async registration, or std::async launch. Later commits 630c618ae7d87bd7bee7979997f31bad7fecd803, 5ff97979fd85db218112f0a69d21fe2f95ef9abc, 7ab6bce7faf0ba466b38a9ed31ccbdadbbd99ecd, 70cdbef69333a5fecd6e9e034d9e1428a544c8a5, and cff6a0acedbc1b8e53aeef118570929b50a711c9 only adjusted wrapping/module APIs or formatting around the already-vulnerable launch and are not introducers.

The BIC dates to 2015-01-06. The Claude/leftibot evidence belongs only to the 2026 fix objects and is excluded by the BIC-only rule.
evidence: First-party lifecycle: https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/issues/632 reports the race, the exact PoC, and ASan's freed-main-thread/read-worker-thread stacks; its final maintainer comment says `Closed in #656`. Consolidation issue https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/issues/655 identifies the async-thread-lifetime issue, and https://github.com/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/pull/656 states that #632 and #636 share the cause: async workers outlive Dispatch_Engine. In the validated clone, reproduce the BIC search with `git log --all --reverse -S'std::async(std::launch::async' -- include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp`: the first hit is 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2 and the only later removal hit is fix 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484. `git log -L 47,56:include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp 1b27d0dd15f45b4781273bc039713a8d8608cf86` follows the vulnerable call through formatting/API-only edits back to 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2. `git show --patch 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2` shows that commit adding `<future>`, future_type, and `std::async(std::launch::async, t_func)` plus the first async test. Direct parent verification: `git show a32a180a063d9186ca38b2708a9c19d50da378db:include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp` shows the file ending after Vector/string/Map/Pair registration, with no future or async code. Release boundary: `git diff v5.5.1 v5.6.0 -- include/chaiscript/chaiscript_stdlib.hpp` is precisely the future/async addition, and `git tag --contains 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2` begins at v5.6.0 and includes every later release through v6.1.0; the advisory independently says versions up to 6.1.0. `git tag --contains 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484` returns no tags, so the closing fix is on post-v6.1.0 develop and is not in a numbered release in this clone. Fix verification: `git show --patch 8dbb5eddcead54ff8b44b6646d491fec921a1720` removes stdlib's untracked std::async registration, moves async registration into ChaiScript_Basic, records each std::thread in Dispatch_Engine, and joins all tracked workers from the engine destructor before shared state is destroyed. GitHub's first-party `/repos/ChaiScript/ChaiScript/pulls/656/commits` endpoint lists 8dbb5eddcead54ff8b44b6646d491fec921a1720 as that direct patch and 530b492b8e1e729b19656f637ca36095f9d98df2 as only the requested rule-of-five follow-up. The project landed them as squash commit 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484; `git show --patch 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484` contains the same lifetime fix. Finally, `git cat-file -p 52d03a66b15358e8fd2caeb5b063044c8aa839d2` provides the complete BIC commit-object AI check and contains no AI marker.
reasoning: The reported comparator UAF is downstream of a clear ownership/lifetime error: introducing script async() made it possible for engine-dependent work to run beyond engine lifetime, while no engine-owned join existed. The first-writer evidence converges: -S identifies the 2015 future-support commit, -L traces the exact surviving launch back to it, its diff adds the full vulnerable facility, and its immediate parent directly lacks it. It is a one-parent atomic feature commit, not a move, revert, release commit, merge, or squash aggregate, so no decomposition is needed. The tag graph establishes v5.6.0 as the first affected numbered release, v5.5.1 as unaffected, and v6.1.0 as the last published numbered tag containing the flaw. The direct PR patch 8dbb5eddcead54ff8b44b6646d491fec921a1720 repairs the root cause by making Dispatch_Engine own and join the workers; squash 7b95ff5126f0365c101b08fa33b50ae387342484 is the closing commit on develop, with no release tag yet. Although the fix was produced by leftibot with an explicit Claude Opus trailer, the protocol permits AI judgment only from the BIC commit object. That 2015 object has a human author/committer and no AI attribution, so the correct closed verdict is NOT_AI.
